text: Appointment Before the toss for innings two Umpires shall be appointed, one for each end, to control the game with absolute impartiality as required by the Laws.

text: The Wickets The Umpires shall satisfy themselves before the start of the match that the wickets are properly pitched.

text: Clock or Watch The Umpires shall agree between themselves and inform both Captains before the start of the match on the watch or clock to be followed during the match.

text: In addition, if during play, the Umpires decide that the light is unfit, only the batting side shall have the option of continuing play.

text: Definition of a Throw A ball shall be deemed to have been thrown if, in the opinion of either Umpire, the process of straightening the bowling arm, whether it be partial or complete, takes place during that part of the delivery swing which directly precedes the ball leaving the hand.

text: Judging a Wide If the Bowler bowls the ball so high over or so wide of the wicket that, in the opinion of the Umpire it passes out of reach of the Striker, standing in a normal guard position, the Umpire shall call and signal “wide ball” as soon as it has passed the line of the Striker’s wicket.

text_norm: the striker has a right, without interference from the fielding side, to make one attempt to hit the ball.

text_norm: runs resulting from a wide all runs which are run or result from a wide ball which is not a no ball shall be scored wide balls, or if no runs are made one shall be scored.

text_norm: wide ball not counting in over a wide ball shall not be reckoned as one of the over - see law 22.3.

text: Byes If the ball, not having been called “wide” or “no ball” passes the Striker without touching his bat or person, and any runs are obtained, the Umpire shall signal “bye” and the run or runs shall be credited as such to the batting side.
text_norm: byes if the ball, not having been called "wide" or "no ball" passes the striker without touching his bat or person, and any runs are obtained, the umpire shall signal "bye" and the run or runs shall be credited as such to the batting side.

text: Leg-Byes If the ball, not having been called “wide” or “no ball” is unintentionally deflected by the Striker’s dress or person, except a hand holding the bat, and any runs are obtained the Umpire shall signal “leg-bye” and the run or runs so scored shall be credited as such to the batting side.
text_norm: leg-byes if the ball, not having been called "wide" or "no ball" is unintentionally deflected by the striker's dress or person, except a hand holding the bat, and any runs are obtained the umpire shall signal "leg-bye" and the run or runs so scored shall be credited as such to the batting side.

text: Such leg-byes shall only be scored if, in the opinion of the Umpire, the Striker has:

text: attempted to play the ball with his bat, or

text: On the call and signal of “dead ball” the Batsmen shall return to their original ends and no runs shall be allowed.
text_norm: on the call and signal of "dead ball" the batsmen shall return to their original ends and no runs shall be allowed.

text_norm: when either umpire has given a batsman not out, the other umpire shall, within his jurisdiction, answer the appeal or a further appeal, provided it is made in time in accordance with 1. above (time of appeals).

text: Consultation by Umpires An Umpire may consult with the other Umpire on a point of fact which the latter may have been in a better position to see and shall then give his decision.
text_norm: consultation by umpires an umpire may consult with the other umpire on a point of fact which the latter may have been in a better position to see and shall then give his decision.

text_norm: if, after consultation, there is still doubt remaining the decision shall be in favour of the batsman.

text: Batsman Leaving his Wicket under a Misapprehension The Umpires shall intervene if satisfied that a Batsman, not having been given out, has left his wicket under a misapprehension that he has been dismissed.
text_norm: batsman leaving his wicket under a misapprehension the umpires shall intervene if satisfied that a batsman, not having been given out, has left his wicket under a misapprehension that he has been dismissed.

text_norm: umpire's decision the umpire's decision is final.

text: He may alter his decision, provided that such alteration is made promptly.
text_norm: he may alter his decision, provided that such alteration is made promptly.

text: Withdrawal of an Appeal In exceptional circumstances the Captain of the fielding side may seek permission of the Umpire to withdraw an appeal providing the outgoing Batsman has not left the playing area.
text_norm: withdrawal of an appeal in exceptional circumstances the captain of the fielding side may seek permission of the umpire to withdraw an appeal providing the outgoing batsman has not left the playing area.

text: If this is allowed, the Umpire shall cancel his decision.

text: Wicket Down The wicket is down if:-
text_norm: wicket down the wicket is down if:-

text: Either the ball or the Striker’s bat or person completely removes either bail from the top of the stumps.
text_norm: either the ball or the striker's bat or person completely removes either bail from the top of the stumps.

text: A disturbance of a bail, whether temporary or not, shall not constitute a complete removal, but the wicket is down if a bail in falling lodges between two of the stumps.
text_norm: a disturbance of a bail, whether temporary or not, shall not constitute a complete removal, but the wicket is down if a bail in falling lodges between two of the stumps.

text: Any player completely removes with his hand or arm a bail from the top of the stumps, providing that the ball is held in that hand or in the hand of the arm so used.
text_norm: any player completely removes with his hand or arm a bail from the top of the stumps, providing that the ball is held in that hand or in the hand of the arm so used.

text: When both bails are off, a stump is struck out of the ground by the ball, or a player strikes or pulls a stump out of the ground, providing that the ball is held in the hand(s) or in the hand of the arm so used.
text_norm: when both bails are off, a stump is struck out of the ground by the ball, or a player strikes or pulls a stump out of the ground, providing that the ball is held in the hand(s) or in the hand of the arm so used.

text: One Bail Off If one bail is off, it shall be sufficient for the purpose of putting the wicket down to remove the remaining bail, or to strike or pull any of the three stumps out of the ground in any of the ways stated in 1. above.
text_norm: one bail off if one bail is off, it shall be sufficient for the purpose of putting the wicket down to remove the remaining bail, or to strike or pull any of the three stumps out of the ground in any of the ways stated in 1. above.

text: All the Stumps Out of the Ground If all the stumps are out of the ground, the fielding side shall be allowed to put back one or more stumps in order to have an opportunity of putting the wicket down.
text_norm: all the stumps out of the ground if all the stumps are out of the ground, the fielding side shall be allowed to put back one or more stumps in order to have an opportunity of putting the wicket down.

text: Dispensing with Bails If owing to the strength of the wind, it has been agreed to dispense with the bails in accordance with Law 8.
text_norm: dispensing with bails if owing to the strength of the wind, it has been agreed to dispense with the bails in accordance with law 8.

text_norm: (dispensing with bails) the decision as to when the wicket is down is one for the umpires to decide on the facts before them.

text: In such circumstances and if the Umpires so decide the wicket shall be held to be down even though a stump has not been struck out of the ground.
text_norm: in such circumstances and if the umpires so decide the wicket shall be held to be down even though a stump has not been struck out of the ground.

text_norm: remaking the wicket if the wicket is broken while the ball is in play, it is not the umpire's duty to remake the wicket until the ball has become dead - see law 23.

text_norm: when out of his ground a batsman shall be considered to be out of his ground unless some part of his bat in his hand or of his person is grounded behind the line of the popping crease.

text: Out Bowled The Striker shall be out bowled if:-
text_norm: out bowled the striker shall be out bowled if:-

text: His wicket is bowled down, even if the ball first touches his bat or person.
text_norm: his wicket is bowled down, even if the ball first touches his bat or person.

text: Out Timed Out An incoming Batsman shall be out Timed Out if he wilfully takes more than two minutes to come in — the two minutes being timed from the moment a wicket falls until the new batsman steps on to the field of play.
text_norm: out timed out an incoming batsman shall be out timed out if he wilfully takes more than two minutes to come in - the two minutes being timed from the moment a wicket falls until the new batsman steps on to the field of play.

text: Entry in Score Book The correct entry in the score book when a Batsman is given out under this Law is “timed out”, and the Bowler does not get credit for the wicket.
text_norm: entry in score book the correct entry in the score book when a batsman is given out under this law is "timed out", and the bowler does not get credit for the wicket.

text: Batsmen Crossing on the Field of Play It is an essential duty of the Captains to ensure that the ingoing Batsman passes the out-going one before the latter leaves the field of play.
text_norm: batsmen crossing on the field of play it is an essential duty of the captains to ensure that the ingoing batsman passes the out-going one before the latter leaves the field of play.

text: A Fair Catch A catch shall be considered to have been fairly made if:-

text: The Fieldsman is within the field of play throughout the act of making the catch.
text_norm: the fieldsman is within the field of play throughout the act of making the catch.

text_norm: the act of making the catch shall start from the time when the fieldsman first handles the ball and shall end when he both retains complete control over the further disposal of the ball and remains within the field of play.

text_norm: in order to be within the field of play, the fieldsman may not touch or ground any part of his person on or over a boundary line.

text: When the boundary is marked by a fence or board the Fieldsman may not ground any part of his person over the boundary fence or board, but may touch or lean over the boundary fence or board in completing the catch.
text_norm: when the boundary is marked by a fence or board the fieldsman may not ground any part of his person over the boundary fence or board, but may touch or lean over the boundary fence or board in completing the catch.

text: The ball is hugged to the body of the catcher or accidentally lodges in his dress or, in the case of the Wicket-Keeper, in his pads.
text_norm: the ball is hugged to the body of the catcher or accidentally lodges in his dress or, in the case of the wicket-keeper, in his pads.

text: However, a Striker may not be caught if a ball lodges in a protective helmet worn by a Fieldsman, in which case the Umpire shall call and signal “dead ball”.

text: (Dead Ball).

text: The ball does not touch the ground even though a hand holding it does so in effecting the catch.
text_norm: the ball does not touch the ground even though a hand holding it does so in effecting the catch.

text: A Fieldsman catches the ball, after it has been lawfully played a second time by the Striker, but only if the ball has not touched the ground since being first struck.
text_norm: a fieldsman catches the ball, after it has been lawfully played a second time by the striker, but only if the ball has not touched the ground since being first struck.

text: A Fieldsman catches the ball after it has touched an Umpire, another Fieldsman or the other Batsman.
text_norm: a fieldsman catches the ball after it has touched an umpire, another fieldsman or the other batsman.

text: However a Striker may not be caught if a ball has touched a protective helmet worn by a Fieldsman.
text_norm: however a striker may not be caught if a ball has touched a protective helmet worn by a fieldsman.

text: The ball is caught off an obstruction within the boundary provided it has not previously been agreed to regard the obstruction as a boundary.
text_norm: the ball is caught off an obstruction within the boundary provided it has not previously been agreed to regard the obstruction as a boundary.

text: Scoring of Runs If a Striker is caught, no runs shall be scored.
text_norm: scoring of runs if a striker is caught, no runs shall be scored.

text: Scoring from an Attempted Catch When a Fieldsman carrying the ball touches or grounds any part of his person on or over a boundary marked by a line, 6 runs shall be scored.

text: Players Damaging the Pitch The Umpires shall intervene and prevent Players from causing damage to the pitch which may assist the Bowlers of either side.
text_norm: players damaging the pitch the umpires shall intervene and prevent players from causing damage to the pitch which may assist the bowlers of either side.

text: See Note (c).
text_norm: see note (c).

text: In the event of any member of the fielding side damaging the pitch the Umpire shall follow the procedure of caution, final warning and reporting as set out in 10(a) above.
text_norm: in the event of any member of the fielding side damaging the pitch the umpire shall follow the procedure of caution, final warning and reporting as set out in 10(a) above.

text: In the event of a Bowler contravening this Law by running down the pitch after delivering the ball, the Umpire at the Bowler’s end shall first caution the Bowler.
text_norm: in the event of a bowler contravening this law by running down the pitch after delivering the ball, the umpire at the bowler's end shall first caution the bowler.

text: If this caution is ineffective the Umpire shall adopt the procedures, other than the calling of “no-ball”, of final warning, action against the Bowler and reporting.
text_norm: if this caution is ineffective the umpire shall adopt the procedures, other than the calling of "no-ball", of final warning, action against the bowler and reporting.

text: In the event of a Batsman damaging the pitch the Umpire at the Bowler’s end shall follow the procedures of caution, final warning and reporting as set out in 10(c) above.
text_norm: in the event of a batsman damaging the pitch the umpire at the bowler's end shall follow the procedures of caution, final warning and reporting as set out in 10(c) above.

text: Batsman Unfairly Stealing a Run Any attempt by the Batsman to steal a run during the Bowler’s run-up is unfair.
text_norm: batsman unfairly stealing a run any attempt by the batsman to steal a run during the bowler's run-up is unfair.

text: Unless the Bowler attempts to run out either Batsman — see Law 24.4.
text_norm: unless the bowler attempts to run out either batsman - see law 24.4.

text: (Bowler Throwing at Striker’s Wicket Before Delivery) and Law 24.5.
text_norm: (bowler throwing at striker's wicket before delivery) and law 24.5.

text: (Bowler Attempting to Run Out Non-Striker Before Delivery) — the Umpire shall call and signal “dead ball” as soon as the Batsmen cross in any such attempt to run.
text_norm: (bowler attempting to run out non-striker before delivery) - the umpire shall call and signal "dead ball" as soon as the batsmen cross in any such attempt to run.

text: The Batsmen shall then return to their original wickets.
text_norm: the batsmen shall then return to their original wickets.

text: Players’ Conduct In the event of a player failing to comply with the instructions of an Umpire, criticising his decisions by word or action, or showing dissent, or generally behaving in a manner which might bring the game into disrepute, the Umpire concerned shall, in the first place report the matter to the other Umpire and to the Player’s Captain requesting the latter to take action.
text_norm: players' conduct in the event of a player failing to comply with the instructions of an umpire, criticising his decisions by word or action, or showing dissent, or generally behaving in a manner which might bring the game into disrepute, the umpire concerned shall, in the first place report the matter to the other umpire and to the player's captain requesting the latter to take action.

text: If this proves ineffective, the Umpire shall report the incident as soon as possible to the Executive of the Player’s team and to any Governing Body responsible for the match, who shall take any further action which is considered appropriate against the Player or Players concerned.
text_norm: if this proves ineffective, the umpire shall report the incident as soon as possible to the executive of the player's team and to any governing body responsible for the match, who shall take any further action which is considered appropriate against the player or players concerned.

text: The Condition of the Ball Umpires shall make frequent and irregular inspections of the condition of the ball.
text_norm: the condition of the ball umpires shall make frequent and irregular inspections of the condition of the ball.

text: Drying of a Wet Ball A wet ball may be dried on a towel or with sawdust.
text_norm: drying of a wet ball a wet ball may be dried on a towel or with sawdust.

text: Danger Area The danger area on the pitch, which must be protected from damage by a Bowler, shall be regarded by the Umpires as the area contained by an imaginary line 4 ft./1.22 m. from the popping crease, and parallel to it, and within two imaginary and parallel lines drawn down the pitch from points on that line 1 ft./30.48 cm. on either side of the middle stump.
text_norm: danger area the danger area on the pitch, which must be protected from damage by a bowler, shall be regarded by the umpires as the area contained by an imaginary line 4 ft./1.22 m. from the popping crease, and parallel to it, and within two imaginary and parallel lines drawn down the pitch from points on that line 1 ft./30.48 cm. on either side of the middle stump.

text: Fast Short Pitched Balls As a guide, a fast short pitched ball is one which pitches short and passes, or would have passed, above the shoulder height of the Striker standing in a normal batting stance at the crease.
text_norm: fast short pitched balls as a guide, a fast short pitched ball is one which pitches short and passes, or would have passed, above the shoulder height of the striker standing in a normal batting stance at the crease.

text: The Bowling of Fast Full Pitches The bowling of one fast, high full pitch shall be considered to be unfair if, in the opinion of the Umpire, it is deliberate, bowled at the Striker, and if it passes or would have passed above the shoulder height of the Striker when standing in a normal batting stance at the crease.
text_norm: the bowling of fast full pitches the bowling of one fast, high full pitch shall be considered to be unfair if, in the opinion of the umpire, it is deliberate, bowled at the striker, and if it passes or would have passed above the shoulder height of the striker when standing in a normal batting stance at the crease.

text: Time Wasting by Batsmen Other than in exceptional circumstances, the Batsman should always be ready to take strike when the Bowler is ready to start his run-up.
text_norm: time wasting by batsmen other than in exceptional circumstances, the batsman should always be ready to take strike when the bowler is ready to start his run-up.
